entries.claim: Task 1 offers the `{param:}` constant as a way to read the switch, but `{param:Name|Default}` only parses the `/Name=Value` form, so it cannot detect a bare `/LAUNCH`, which is the switch name the plan fixes.
entries.failure_scenario: Suppose the executor picks the plan's `{param:LAUNCH|...}` option and the smoke runs `setup.exe /VERYSILENT /LAUNCH`. The constant returns its default whether or not the switch is present, so the Check never admits the launch. No app starts, and Task 3 dies at its 'not exactly one process' lookup instead of at the address check. The bite-proof push is spent, and the work goes back to the owner on a mechanism the plan itself recommended. Only the `ParamCount`/`ParamStr` route works for a bare switch.

entries.claim: Task 4 says to change nothing else in the README, but `README.md:192` has the same stale sentence for the Mac app ('It is reachable from that Mac only.'). It contradicts the same `HQPTUNER_LISTEN_HOST` table row (`README.md:238`) that D-09 cites, and `packaging/macos/smoke.sh:61-63` requires `LSEnvironment.HQPTUNER_LISTEN_HOST` to be `0.0.0.0`. This is a second instance of the same stale-copy defect, which `~/dev/CLAUDE.md` 10.2 puts in scope or makes a 6.1 boundary question; the plan does neither.
entries.failure_scenario: Execute Task 4 as written: its `grep -c "reachable from that PC only"` check prints 0 and the task passes. The README still tells Mac users their app works only on that Mac, while the table two sections down says the macOS app binds `0.0.0.0`. The phase ships the same contradiction it set out to remove, and no task or verify step catches it.
